userStories.title: Add consistent empty states, loading skeletons, and error states to all list pages

userStories.title: Unify snake_case to camelCase data transformation with centralized entity mappers
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a single transformation layer between API responses (snake_case) and frontend state (camelCase) so every page doesn't duplicate 50+ lines of field mapping.
acceptanceCriteria: Create client/src/lib/entity-mappers.ts with typed mapper functions for each entity: mapLead, mapCustomer, mapQuote, mapInvoice, mapOrder, mapContact, mapEquipment
Each mapper converts snake_case API fields to camelCase TypeScript interfaces with correct types
Each mapper provides sensible defaults for nullable fields (empty string for text, 0 for numbers, null for optional relations)
Create a generic mapResponse<T>(response, mapper) utility that handles both single and array responses
Integrate mappers into apiRequest or create entity-specific query hooks that auto-transform
Refactor at least 8 major pages (Leads, Customers, Quotes, Invoices, Orders, Contacts, Contracts, Equipment) to use centralized mappers
Remove duplicate inline transformation code from refactored pages
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Every page currently does manual field mapping like: invoiceNumber: item.invoiceNumber || item.invoice_number || ''. This creates 50+ lines of duplicate transformation per page, is error-prone, and makes it hard to add new fields. A centralized mapper eliminates this entirely.

userStories.title: Implement optimistic mutations for inline edits and status changes
userStories.description: As a user editing records, I need the UI to update immediately when I make changes rather than waiting for the server round-trip so the app feels fast and responsive.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a useOptimisticMutation hook that wraps TanStack Query's useMutation with optimistic cache updates
On mutation: immediately update the query cache with the expected new value
On success: merge the server response into the cache (server is source of truth for computed fields)
On error: roll back the optimistic update, show error toast, restore previous state
Apply to inline cell edits in table views (status changes, field updates)
Apply to drag-and-drop stage changes on pipeline boards
Apply to toggle operations (active/inactive, pin/unpin, archive/unarchive)
Show a subtle 'Saving...' indicator near the edited field during the API call
Batch rapid edits: if user edits multiple fields within 500ms, debounce into a single PATCH request
Typecheck passes: npm run check
Build passes: npm run build
userStories.notes: Currently pages use queryClient.invalidateQueries() which does a full refetch after every mutation. This causes visible loading flicker and feels slow, especially on mobile. useOptimisticMutations hook already exists in the codebase but isn't widely adopted. This story expands adoption.
